contract.scope_decision: The attestation rule is scoped to the validation tranche; authoring resumes are development loops and are exempt, pinned by TestAuthoringResumeIsExemptFromTheAttestationRule.

fixed_after_fourth_review: N1: the corpus test checked one direction only - verifyClosureReviewVerdictLine returns nil exactly when closureReviewVerdict yields ACCEPT, so the false-refusal guard inside the error branch was unreachable, while three records claimed the corpus arbitrated both directions. Ground truth is now a committed expectations table at artifacts/closure-verdict-corpus-expectations.json, derived by a scan independent of the runner implementation, and the test compares the parser against it in both directions with the per-verdict counts pinned.

N2: the verdict-list rejection used a three-field window fitted to how this repository happens to order the words in its prompt boilerplate; reordering two words defeated it and made an evaluator prompt read as an accepting record. It is replaced by an order-independent rule: a verdict token followed by a comma or a slash, with another verdict word anywhere later on the line, is an enumeration. A token followed by prose remains a statement, so a record may cite another round verdict on the same line - which the fourth reviewer prescription would have wrongly refused, as the third review own record demonstrates.

N3: the parser now tracks block context. Fenced blocks, block quotes and indented blocks are skipped, the block-quote marker is removed from the furniture cutset, and a separator is required between the label and the token, so a verdict quoted from another record or used in a sentence is no longer read as this record own.

N4: the furniture cutset admits em and en dashes, footnote brackets, carriage returns and non-breaking spaces, and the boundary document now states the accepted verdict-statement forms so the closure record author writes one the frozen parser reads.
N5: the corpus is pinned rather than swept from the live docs/reviews directory, so a review record added by unrelated later work can no longer turn a frozen test red.
N6: the corpus count in the candidate note is corrected.
fixed_after_third_review: P1-N1: the closure verdict parser was wrong in both directions against this project own corpus - it refused 17 of the 19 records written in the dominant code-span style because the trim cutset omitted the backtick, refused the heading-then-token house style, refused an accepting record citing an earlier REVISE, and accepted 12 non-records including five evaluator prompts matching the instruction that lists the available verdicts. It is rewritten structurally: furniture-only prefix with a closed qualifier set, lone-token extraction with non-letters trimmed, heading-then-next-line support, verdict-list rejection, and first-statement-decisive. The committed review corpus is now the arbiter in code via TestClosureVerdictParserAgreesWithTheCommittedReviewCorpus, which fails if any evaluator prompt reads as an accepting record or any record stating ACCEPT is refused.
P3-N1 new-b: the boundary document now enumerates the attestation exact JSON field set, which decodeStrict enforces and which previously appeared only in the candidate note and the runner source.
P3-N1 new-c: the boundary document records the one unresumable state, a custodian process that wrote its start event but died before its first checkpoint.
P3-N1 new-d: the stale round-count text in this inventory is corrected.
fixed_after_second_review: P2-N1: the interrupted_at anchor gains the same five-minute skew allowance its counterpart already carried. A signalled interruption stamps its termination entry after the signal arrives, so without the allowance an honest attestation of a host restart or process kill was refused - a defect the first payload could not have had, because it wrote no termination entry that survived.

P2-N2: the boundary document and README now state the interrupted_at anchor, the fact that the 72 hours are measured from the last log entry, and the one-hour authorization freshness bound, the last explicitly labelled an implementation control rather than a section 9 requirement.

P3-N2: partialArtifactDigests drops omitempty for a fixed four-key shape, the admitted digest key set covers all four, and the fixture now sets grader and Arm B digests so the guard sees the validation-path shape.
P3-N3: the closure record must carry a verdict line stating ACCEPT, and a REVISE verdict line refuses; matching the bare token accepted this project own committed REVISE records.
P3-N4: a test now pins the branch that refuses an attestation authored at resume time for a weeks-old interruption, the branch that actually closes P2-3.

P3-N5: watchProcessTerminationOn takes the signal channel directly, so the stop behaviour and the live-progress wiring are exercised on every host instead of skipping on Windows; SIGTERM exit 143 is pinned too.
P3-N6: the error-path stop event carries the real cumulative spend instead of zero.
P3-N7: the dead assignment in the resume-counter test is removed.
P3-N8: processEventLog.append is serialized by a mutex, so the run loop and the signal goroutine cannot interleave a line.
P3-N9: the lapse explanation is required only past a one-hour promptness window, so it marks a real lapse instead of being demanded on every resume.
P3-N10: the gocyclo claim in this inventory is corrected to name runScheduledCases and validateExternalGrade at 14.
fixed: P1-1: the termination handler now stops the process (exit 128+signal) after recording, so a signalled run cannot keep launching while the log asserts a termination; watchProcessTerminationWith takes an injectable exit so the stop behaviour itself is tested.

P1-2: the single-resume counter is corroborated against the append-only process-event log, which carries one start entry per custodian process; a checkpoint edited downward, or a deleted or unreadable log, refuses the resume.
P2-1: the outcome-free field-set guard descends into artifact_digests with its own admitted key set and requires arm_assignment_counts keys to be Phase 1 arms.
P2-2: TestScheduledResumePersistsTheResumeCounter exercises the counter round trip end to end and pins the refusal of a checkpoint claiming two resumes.
P2-3: the resume window is anchored to the last process-event timestamp and to the runner clock, so back-dating an interruption or presenting a stale authorization is refused.
P2-4: the closure record must be a non-empty regular markdown file under docs/reviews that states an ACCEPT verdict, not merely an existing path.
P2-5: verifyResumeAttestationFields is split into identity and condition halves, restoring complexity headroom.
P2-6: the production termination event carries live progress through a mutex-guarded liveProgress handle instead of a hardcoded zero.
P3-3: the stop event records a fixed stop-kind token instead of the raw failure text, which could quote a per-trial status.
P3-4: the added gate fields are indented consistently with the block before the refreeze pins them.
P3-7: a missing live schedule or world-build digest now refuses rather than skipping the comparison.
P3-8: verifyAcceptedLocalArtifacts is hoisted above the runner-freeze check so payload commits keep exercising it.
P3-9: an evidence-write failure records a terminal stop event, so the log is never ambiguous between an error exit and an abrupt kill.
carried: P2-5 successor: verifyResumeAttestationFields is split into identity and condition halves and now measures below 5. runScheduledCases and validateExternalGrade remain at gocyclo 14, both pre-existing and unchanged by this payload.

accepted_residuals: Neither supported host exposes the sending principal of a signal to a Go handler, so a termination event records exposed=false with the reason; establishing that no project participant initiated a kill remains the custodian written attestation, as section 9 requires.
